findings.description: Negative case: the acknowledgement for noshow-charge-authority is spoken in the _inbox/ transcript under grooming, and no prior note carries an equivalent naming.
findings.evidence: tests/fixtures/inbox-to-memory/evals/unacknowledged-tension/_inbox/2026-04-22-bexley-carrier-review.md:11-13 — "Then Terry stopped the meeting. / 'Before we write another line about no-shows — who signs off on charging a carrier for a missed appointment? I asked it on the walkthrough in February. I asked it at the slot rules workshop. Iris put it on the steerco agenda in March and it came back the way it went in. Same question every time, and it has never once had an answer.'" Reinforced at :29 — "the charge question, again, with nobody's name against it". I grepped every fixture file for who signs|who owns|charge|billing|authority|invoice and read each hit: the only prior-note hits are the [open question: noshow-charge-authority] token lines themselves (which are the recurrence, not an acknowledgement), two [memory candidate: project] claims about the report's recipient (2026-02-11:41, 2026-04-08:43), and one action item at 2026-02-25:42 ("@Iris — find out who owns a carrier charge on the Meridian side"). That last is the question being routed at the time, not a speaker naming it as chronically unanswered; nothing in any prior note asserts the question has stayed open. The distinguishing acknowledgement exists in exactly one place, the transcript process mode reads.

findings.description: Interference check: no _inbox/ file names the positive slug's question aloud, verified by reading the transcript end to end against what after-hours-gate-cover actually asks, not by keyword search.
findings.evidence: Positive slug's question (notes/2026-02-11-...:36): "[open question: after-hours-gate-cover] Who staffs the Bexley gate when the appointment day runs past 18:00? | blocks: the phase 2 extended windows | default: the day-shift lead stays late and nobody has agreed to pay for it". I read all 30 lines of the sole _inbox/ file. Its subjects are: the three-week no-show count and its carrier split (:7), Crestline's dispatch board carrying the customer's delivery window instead of the appointment (:9), the charge-authority acknowledgement (:11-19), the 30-minute grace window holding with two trucks worked in at 28 and 29 minutes past (:21), carrier-code fragmentation on the report (:23), and three closing items (:27-29: carrier-code mapping, Dwight's hand-copy, the charge question). None of these is the after-hours question paraphrased: nothing addresses who is at the gate when the day runs long, evening or extended-window coverage, shift end, or unpaid overtime — the meeting itself runs 09:15 to 10:35 (:3). The nearest surface-level neighbours are about clock times inside the grace window and about a delivery-window mismatch, neither of which asks who staffs the gate. A corroborating grep for staff|shift|after.hour|18:00|six o|evening|night|late|overtime|end of the day|cover|hours|extended window over the _inbox/ file returned no matches (exit 1).

'v1 files: 0' is what makes the lint's token pass load-bearing here: lint-scope.sh:413-431 only pushes schema-carrying files into v2_files, and all 7 qualify, so no file's tokens went unread. The derived v2 counts the lint checks are also consistent by inspection (open_questions 2/3/3/2 and resolved_questions 0/0/0/1 across the four notes, matching the token counts above).

findings.description: Well-formedness part (b): the by-hand token grammar pass, run independently over note bodies, agrees with the lint — every surviving token is a registered shape.
findings.evidence: I replicated the four steps rather than trusting (a): skipped CLAUDE.md/README.md (none present), took only extract_body's slice per lint-scope.sh:208-216, stripped [[...]] per :218-222, then read the bracketed tokens (listing above). Every survivor matches the grammar table at inbox-to-memory/references/machine-contracts.md:69-78 — [memory candidate: project] (:69), [memory candidate: client] (:70), [open question: <slug>] (:75), [open question resolved: <slug>] (:76), [decision: one-way|two-way] with 'two-way' inside the enumerated set (:78). '[ ]' is the markdown checkbox and is not token-shaped under the linter's own regex '\[[a-z][a-z0-9 -]*(:|\])'. The three _memory/ records yield no tokens at all. Correctly excluded by the scoping and not read as tokens: frontmatter 'related: [extends::0Z0zEXm85o]', 'tags:'/'topics:'/'entities:' flow lists, 'source_refs: [dyFsn16vEe]', and the wiki links [[bexley-dock-capacity-MH-2ub4mwK|memory]], [[appointment-window-tolerance-AJ8Ia-Z8Xg|memory]], [[bexley-pilots-first-LvJedcverX|memory]]. Parts (a) and (b) agree: no ungrammatical token by either route.
